findings.change: The integration requirement now has an explicit decision boundary for the current head H. Route 1 (collect normally) applies when G1 has passed on H and a dispatched review or a candidate CI run is actually in flight; results are collected within their timeouts and the integration finding joins that same-version batch (FIN-03). Route 2 applies otherwise, including G1 not passed, review not dispatched, a conflicted PR with no CI run for H, or in-flight work timed out or definitively unavailable. Route 2 immediately uses the existing pre_review_g1 mechanism with reason base_integration. It dispatches no new G2 on H, does not wait for conflict-suppressed CI, and records G3 on H as unknown(ci_unavailable_conflict), never success. Both routes use one writer, confirmed stopped per §6/D47 before dispatch (unknown means stop or Blocked). Both use one batch with one round counted on actual dispatch. Obsolete H results are kept as history and received findings are preserved. The new H needs fresh full G1/G2/G3. The integration finding (source=base_integration) has a stable ID from (base repo/branch, pinned base tip, H); it deduplicates repeated triggers into one open batch and is the Red binding target. Closure still follows F04. No new trigger, platform or lifecycle is added.

findings.source: review-01 new, major, blocking for design
findings.change: The integration assignment pins the prior head H and the exact base tip B fetched read-only. It separately authorizes (1) unchanged import of B's changes relative to merge-base(H,B) and (2) author edits, limited to conflicted paths plus the batch findings' approved scope. The merge commit M must have parents exactly [H, B] with H first. The controller recomputes `git merge-tree --write-tree H B`, stores the auto-merge tree and conflicted paths in provenance, and classifies each path of M as unchanged import, authored conflict resolution, or authored extra edit. This uses existing git objects only, with no semantic-diff framework or per-file registry. Authored edits must stay in scope. An unrelated edit hidden in the import differs from the auto-merge result and is rejected, and an out-of-scope resolution goes to D11. Pure import needs no upstream Red and makes no N/A claim; prior task Reds stay traceable through first-parent lineage. A behavioral authored resolution needs an original Red bound to the integration finding and batch; a non-behavioral one uses N/A eligibility. The new H still needs Green/regression, full G2 and G3.
